newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus welcomes Euro parliament decision on Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus welcomes Euro parliament decision on Turkey.

text.p: Cyprus on Thursday said the European Parliament was "fully justified" in freezing European Union financial aid to Ankara as punishment for Turkey's failure to improve its human rights record.
"The decision was, in broad terms reasonable and fully justified," Cypriot foreign minister Alecos Michaelides told Reuters.

"The message one receives, not Turkey but everyone, is that if financial assistance is required they have to show respect for fundamental fights," he said, adding the move should be seen as a constructive one by Turkey for it to try to improve its record.
Turkey has occupied the northern third of Cyprus since July 1974 after an invasion sparked by a short-lived coup engineered by the military regime ruling in Greece at the time.

In a first reading of the 1997 EU budget, the parliament, angered by Turkey's human rights record, voted to block hundreds of millions of dollars of aid to help Ankara set up a customs union with the European Union.
The parliament will take a second and final reading of the 1997 EU budget in December.

Turkey's Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller pledged last week to clean up Turkey's human rights performance, saying the government would cut the period of detention in custody and make changes to the State Security Court system.

The European Parliament approved the customs union last December only after the Ankara government had given explicit guarantees that it would take positive action on human rights, democratisation, Cyprus and the plight of the Kurds.
But the Euro MPs complained that Turkey had failed to honour these commitments.

"To accommodate Turkey in occupied Cyprus for 22 years, to accommodate the recent murders and the gross violations of human rights is not to the benefit of Turkey. It is a clear signal to respect the territorial integrity of their neighbours," Michaelides said.
